source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 19, Table A (MFJ or QSS column, more than 59,000 to 60,000: 12,000); PDF page 20, Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule); PDF page 23, Table E (MFJ/QSS, more than 52,000 to 96,000: .10); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 60,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 28,500.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 60,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 60,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 60,000.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 60,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 60,000.00 is more than 59,000.00, exemption 12,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 60,000.00 - 12,000.00 = 48,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 48,000.00: 20,000.00 x 0.02 + 28,000.00 x 0.045 = 400.00 + 1,260.00 = 1,660.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 60,000.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 1,660.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 60,000.00 is in the band more than 52,000.00); Line 9 = 1,660.00 x 0.10 = 166.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 1,660.00 - 166.00 = 1,494.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: A qualifying surviving spouse uses the MFJ/QSS columns of Tables A and E and the joint Table B schedule.
